name: Miharu Takizakura
aliases: 三春滝桜（ベニシダレザクラ）
description: Miharu Takizakura is a roughly 1,000-year-old weeping cherry (beni-shidare-zakura) in Miharu town, designated a National Natural Monument and one of Japan's Three Great Cherry Trees. In mid-April its cascading branches burst into a waterfall of pink blossoms.
highlights: One of Japan's Three Great Cherry Trees
notes: Viewing fee ¥500 during the peak season (middle-school age and under free). Blossoms peak around mid-April; the tree is illuminated at night during the season. About 15 min by bus from JR Miharu Station (Ban-etsu East Line) or 20 min by car from Joban Expressway Funahiki-Miharu IC. Best visited with flexible timing as bloom dates shift yearly.
parking: Paid parking near the tree (peak season)

en.name: Miharu Takizakura

ja.name: 三春滝桜
ja.description: 樹齢1,000年以上と推定されるベニシダレザクラの巨木で、国の天然記念物。日本三大桜の一つに数えられ、4月中旬には枝垂れ桜の花が滝のように咲き誇ります。
ja.notes: 見頃の時期のみ観桜料500円（中学生以下無料）。三春駅からバス約15分。
